Acme Bio Announces FDA Acceptance of Biologics License Application for Pegozafermin in MASH

PDUFA target action date set; Phase 3 RAINIER topline data on track

SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., October 14, 2026 -- Acme Bio, Inc. (NASDAQ: ACMB), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for liver and metabolic diseases, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted its Biologics License Application (BLA) for pegozafermin for the treatment of adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis.

The FDA has assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of August 28, 2027.

Topline data from the Phase 3 RAINIER trial of pegozafermin, guided for the second half of 2027, have been rescheduled.

Topline data from the Phase 3 RAINIER trial of pegozafermin, guided for the second half of 2027, were delayed to 2028.

Topline data from the Phase 3 RAINIER trial of pegozafermin, guided for the second half of 2027, were moved to 2028.

Topline data from the Phase 3 RAINIER trial of pegozafermin, guided for the second half of 2027, were withdrawn from guidance.

“The acceptance of our BLA brings us one step closer to a new option for people living with MASH,” said Jane Doe, Chief Executive Officer of Acme Bio.

About Pegozafermin

Pegozafermin is an investigational glycoPEGylated analog of fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) being developed for MASH and severe hypertriglyceridemia.

About Acme Bio

Acme Bio, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing pegozafermin and zentocel for liver and metabolic diseases. For more information, visit www.acmebio.example.
